edit.description: matchesAny/globToRegex (473-483) move to a shared home so a second consumer can call them - src/paths.ts is the path-shaped module that already exists; builtinGates imports them back
receives the glob matcher as its shared home

ship detection (1596-1599) matches commitTouchedPaths against declaredPaths via the shared matcher instead of Array.includes - the same semantics the entry-scope write guard at 2060 already applies to the same declaredPaths(entry) list
the agreement pin - a glob-declaring entry whose commit touches a real matching file ships instead of landing channel-only
changelogGate requires a line on any src/-touching commit

summary: Ship detection compares declared paths to commit paths with literal equality while the entry-scope write guard glob-matches the same list - a glob-declaring entry lands on trunk but never drains.

per.section: The fix lands at the mechanism

tests.asserts: a fanout entry declaring a glob (e.g. nodes/territory-*.json) whose worktree commit touches a real matching file (nodes/territory-01.json) is reported merged and removed from pending.json - fails on the pre-fix tree, where Array.includes returns false and the entry is logged channel-only while its commit stays on trunk

acceptance: One glob matcher serves both the entry-scope write guard and ship detection; a glob-declaring entry that touches a matching file ships and drains; a commit touching only channel paths still lands channel-only; tsc/vitest green.
notes: Downstream report (0.9.0 dist), re-verified here. declaredPaths(entry) has two consumers that both judge real commit paths and disagree: Dispatcher.ts:2060 hands it to writablePathsGate as globs; Dispatcher.ts:1596-1599 compares it with Array.includes. Effect is a non-draining loop - commit on trunk, entry still pickable, next tick redoes landed work. matchesAny is module-private today, so sharing needs the move.
